full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the judgment and, decree dated 20-8-97 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh, in Other Class Appeal No. 39 of 1995 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 30-11-94 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Gafargaon, Mymensingh, in Other Class Suit No.54 of 1994 should not be set aside. 

 13. The learned trial Court, without considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on, record and also the legal point involved in this case, particularly Article 52 of the Dhaka University Ordinance, 1973 read with section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure, decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff. 

 14. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 30-11-94 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Gafargaon, Mymensingh, in Other Class Suit No. 54 of 1994, the defendants preferred an appeal before the learned District Judge, Mymensingh which was transferred and heard by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh, in Other Class Appeal No. 39 of 1995 who dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the learned trial Court stating, inter alia, that the learned trial Court did not commit any error or illegality in passing the judgment and also considered the evidence on record by applying his judicial mind. The defendant-appellant-petitioner, being aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate Court affirming the judgment and decree of the trial Court, filed the instant revisional application before the High Court Division. 

 But the plaintiff did not approach any authority of the Ministry of Education or Vice-Chancellor if at all she had any grievance. If the plaintiff Shikha Rani Roy would submit an appeal in the form of petition before the Chancellor of Dhaka University stating all the facts and her grievances instead of filing a suit for declaration she would get redress, but without exhausting the forum empowering the Chancellor under Article 52 of the University Ordinance to hear an appeal and complaint and to do justice she filed the instant suit. The learned Counsel next submits that according to section 9 read with section 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure the suit for declaration is not maintainable because in a suit for simple declaration without seeking consequential relief will be an unexecutable decree. The learned Counsel next submits that the learned trial Court as well as the lower appellate Court did not consider the evidence on record, particularly the evidence of DW 3, the Controller of Examinations, who categorically stated that the letter issued on 8-1-92 was written under duress and on the following day i.e. on 9-1-92, a rejoinder letter was given, but both the Courts failed to appreciate the contents of the letter dated 9-1-92 and gave emphasis on the contents of the letter dated 8-1-92 and, as such, committed an error by misreading the evidence affecting the merit of the case. Further, both the Courts below stated in their judgment that admittedly if 42 marks was added she would pass in 2nd Division but nowhere in the evidence of DWs is it admitted that she obtained 42 marks. Rather they categorically stated that she did not appear in her Viva-Voce examination, so the question of obtaining 42 marks is an imaginary and perverse finding. 

 19. In view of the discussion made above and the facts and circumstances of the case the impugned judgment and decree dated 20-8-1997 in Other Class Appeal No. 39 of 1995 and affirming the judgment and decree dated 30-11-1994 of the trial Court are set aside. The suit of the plaintiff-respondent-opposite party is dismissed.
